intro.headline: AI Supply Chain Software
intro.subtitle: Intelligence that moves your supply chain

modules.name: Shipping Rules Engine
modules.tag: Codify shipping logic — and let qualifying orders book themselves

problem.heading: Every rep ships by their own playbook.
problem.body: Which carrier for hazmat, when a guaranteed service is required, which account to bill — that logic lives in people's heads. New hires guess, veterans improvise, and every routine order still waits on a human to click ship.

benefit.heading: Turn tribal knowledge into rules that fire automatically.
bullets: Route by weight, value, destination, hazmat, customer or SLA
Big-box and collect freight route to the customer's carrier and account automatically
Force guaranteed service on critical lanes; block non-compliant carriers
Auto dispatch: orders that satisfy a rule quote, book and label with no human touch
Crawl-walk-run — automate the low-hanging lanes first, then widen the rules

demo.caption: A routing rule is defined once — then quotes, books and dispatches every qualifying shipment on its own.

roi.proof: Policy is enforced on every shipment automatically — and the orders that qualify never wait on a person.

ev.src: Rules engine — platform capability. Anchor Distributing target: 80–90% hands-off auto-ship.

modules.name: Carrier Management
modules.tag: Every carrier and account, centrally controlled

problem.heading: Your carrier network lives in a spreadsheet — and someone's inbox.
problem.body: Accounts, credentials, contracted rates and service rules are scattered across files and people. Onboarding a carrier is a project, and auditing who got used and why is nearly impossible.

benefit.heading: Run every carrier and account from one place.
bullets: 1,500+ in-house carrier integrations — parcel, LTL, FTL, ocean and air
Load contracted rates, fuel surcharges and rate sheets for carriers without an API
Add or swap carriers without an EDI project or IT ticket
Carrier ratings on claims and on-time so cheapest isn't automatically best
Control which carriers each site, user or lane can use

demo.caption: Add a regional LTL carrier and turn it live across every site in minutes.

roi.statLabel: carrier and system connections, built in-house
roi.proof: No aggregator in the middle — faster data, fewer failures, and no per-transaction toll.

ev.src: 1,500+ connections built in-house, no aggregator. Verifiable in the integrations catalog.

modules.name: Rate Shopping
modules.tag: Compare every carrier and mode in one screen

problem.heading: Nobody knows what the cheapest option was.
problem.body: Rating means portals, phone calls and PDFs. Under time pressure the team ships with whoever answered first, and the savings are invisible because no one ever saw the alternatives.

benefit.heading: Every rate, every mode, side by side — in one screen.
bullets: Parcel, LTL, truckload and international rated from the same page
Contracted, negotiated and program rates all compared together
Transit days, guaranteed options and accessorials shown with the price
Adjust weight or dims and re-rate in place — no going back a screen
The system tells you which carriers didn't rate, and why

demo.caption: One order rated across every connected carrier and mode at once.

roi.proof: Rate shopping and invoice audit are the two largest line items in customer savings models.

ev.src: G2 review · Francisco A.
ev.quote: Saved us a TON of money in both shipment costs and payroll costs due to the saved time.

modules.name: Spot Quoting & Bid Portal
modules.tag: One request out, every bid back in one place

problem.heading: Finding a truck means emailing ten carriers.
problem.body: Every spot load starts a round of individual emails, then a scramble to compare replies buried in an inbox. Nothing is apples-to-apples, nothing is auditable, and the load waits.

benefit.heading: Bid one load to a whole network in a single click.
bullets: Spot quote groups by region, equipment or lane — ping the network, not one rep
Requests can go out automatically the moment an order lands, based on its destination
Carriers bid in a scoped portal — no login, only the details you choose to share
Require a quote number and a cost breakdown: freight, fuel, accessorials
Bids land beside your API and contracted rates for a true side-by-side

demo.caption: One load bid to an East Coast group — responses land next to the API rates.

roi.statLabel: to bid an entire carrier network
roi.proof: Spot bids stop living in an inbox and become a comparable, auditable record.

ev.src: Spot quote module — platform capability.

modules.name: Address Validator & Accessorials
modules.tag: Catch the surcharge before the carrier does

problem.heading: The accessorial shows up on the invoice.
problem.body: A residential delivery quoted as commercial. A liftgate nobody flagged. The quote looked right, the invoice didn't, and by then the margin on that shipment is gone.

benefit.heading: Validate the stop and the service before you rate it.
bullets: Addresses validated at entry — origin and destination, US, Canada and Mexico
Residential and liftgate flagged automatically, and only when the freight warrants it
Dock, appointment and inside-delivery conditions surfaced before booking
Accessorials priced into the quote so the invoice matches what you approved
Defaults per customer or location for the exceptions you already know about

demo.caption: A pallet to a residential stop auto-flags residential and liftgate before rating.

roi.proof: Accessorials caught at quote time are the difference between a quoted rate and a real one.

ev.src: No customer metric yet. Modeled from your LTL count × surprise-charge rate.

modules.name: Shipment Consolidation
modules.tag: Combine orders into fewer, fuller loads

problem.heading: Orders ship the moment they drop — one box at a time.
problem.body: Same-day, same-destination orders leave as separate parcels or half-empty LTL loads. You pay minimums and per-shipment fees over and over for freight that could have moved together.

benefit.heading: The system finds the loads that belong together.
bullets: Same-destination and same-customer orders surfaced as consolidation candidates
Hypothetical consolidation: hold and combine until a weight or capacity target is hit
Multi-stop opportunities flagged during order entry, not after booking
Consolidated freight rated and booked as one shipment, one BOL
Each original order keeps its own tracking and writeback

demo.caption: Four same-city orders combine into one LTL load — and one bill.

roi.proof: One shipment instead of three means one minimum, one booking and one invoice to audit.

ev.src: No customer metric yet. Modeled from consolidatable pairs × your LTL minimum.

modules.name: Pooling & Cross-Dock
modules.tag: Truckload the long haul, LTL the last mile

problem.heading: Every small order pays for its own long haul.
problem.body: Twenty LTL shipments to the same region each buy their own linehaul. The freight is going to the same place — you're just paying twenty times to get it there.

benefit.heading: Pool the region, break it down locally.
bullets: Group regional orders onto one truckload to a cross-dock or pool point
Final mile released as LTL or local delivery from the pool
Every child shipment tracked under the parent move — no hand-off blind spots
Works for two-leg flows where a partner warehouse reworks freight
Compare pooled cost against shipping each order direct

demo.caption: Twenty Northeast orders pool onto one linehaul, then break to LTL final mile.

roi.proof: Pooling converts a pile of LTL minimums into one truckload rate plus short local moves.

ev.src: No customer metric yet. Modeled as linehaul + final mile vs. n × LTL.

modules.name: Multi-Leg Shipments
modules.tag: Plan and track door-to-door, every leg

problem.heading: One shipment becomes three disconnected records.
problem.body: Drayage, linehaul and final mile each live in a different system with a different reference number. Nobody can answer where the freight is without opening three screens and doing math.

benefit.heading: One record spans every leg and every carrier.
bullets: Build ocean, drayage, linehaul and final mile as legs of one move
Each leg gets its own movement ID, carrier, rate and documents
Status rolls up to one shipment timeline
Handoffs are visible — you see the gap before the customer does
Total landed cost accumulates across legs

demo.caption: Track a port-to-door move across three carriers on one timeline.

roi.proof: One shipment record spans drayage, linehaul and final mile — no hand-off blind spots.

ev.src: Ocean, air and drayage on one shipment record — platform capability.

modules.name: Batch Shipping
modules.tag: Rate, label and book hundreds at once

problem.heading: Peak days mean one label at a time.
problem.body: When volume spikes, your team rate-shops, labels and books orders individually — the same clicks, hundreds of times. Throughput is capped by headcount, and errors climb with fatigue.

benefit.heading: Process the whole queue in one pass.
bullets: Select hundreds of orders and rate-shop, label and book them together
Labels print in the order you selected them — no re-sorting at the printer
Large batches supported without the print-count errors of legacy tools
Exceptions pulled out for review instead of stopping the batch
Throughput scales with volume, not with headcount

demo.caption: An entire batch rate-shopped, labeled and booked in a single pass.

roi.statLabel: to book and dispatch an entire batch
roi.proof: Throughput scales with order volume, not headcount. One G2 reviewer bulk-quotes hundreds of locations from a single screen.

ev.src: G2 review · Catherine C.
ev.quote: I spend many many hours quoting customers with hundreds or thousands of locations… This feature alone has saved me days of work in the last couple of months.

modules.name: Parcel Shipping
modules.tag: Every parcel carrier rated on the same screen as freight

problem.heading: Parcel lives in its own system.
problem.body: A separate tool for parcel means a separate login, separate rates and no way to ask the only question that matters on a borderline order: should this go parcel or LTL? Dimensional rules quietly decide it for you.

benefit.heading: One screen for parcel, LTL and truckload.
bullets: Rate parcel against LTL on the same order and pick the cheaper mode
Dimensional weight applied per carrier so the gray-area orders price honestly
Multi-carrier parcel accounts, labels and manifests from one place
Return labels and default return processing built in
Batch parcel days handled from the same queue as freight

demo.caption: A 23 lb order rated parcel and LTL side by side — DIM rules included.

roi.proof: Mode choice becomes a priced comparison instead of a habit.

ev.src: Parcel included at no additional cost — verifiable in any quote.

modules.name: Documents & BOL Control
modules.tag: Every document generated, printed and correctable

problem.heading: The paperwork is assembled by hand.
problem.body: BOLs, packing lists, pallet labels and manifests get built in separate places, printed from separate screens, and corrected with a pen. When a weight changes after pickup, the document and the invoice disagree.

benefit.heading: Generate it all at ship time — and fix it after.
bullets: BOL, packing list, pallet labels and manifests produced on booking
Customer-specific and third-party BOL formats for big-box routing requirements
Documents route to the right printer by user or station
Edit a BOL after the fact — weight, class, mode — with permissioned, tracked changes
PRO number blocks assigned electronically instead of from a sticker sheet

demo.caption: A variable-weight load re-weighed after pickup — BOL corrected, record updated.

roi.proof: Reconciled weights on the BOL are what make the invoice audit defensible.

ev.src: BOL, labels and paperwork from one booking — platform capability.

modules.name: Fleet & Dispatch
modules.tag: Your trucks and your carriers on one board

problem.heading: The dispatch plan is a whiteboard and a phone.
problem.body: Assets, drivers and daily trips are tracked by hand. When a customer closes early or a load moves to tomorrow, someone re-plans on the fly and calls everyone affected — if they remember.

benefit.heading: Plan the day by dragging loads onto trucks.
bullets: Equipment profiles with weight and capacity tolerances and max daily trips
Assign a truck, driver, tracking device or warehouse to any asset
Drag a load between trucks or to another day — the carrier is notified
Same board for owned assets and third-party carriers
ELD and telematics feeds push assignments to the driver's phone

demo.caption: A Monday load drags to Tuesday — the truck and the carrier both update.

roi.proof: Re-planning a day is a drag-and-drop, not a round of phone calls.

ev.src: No customer metric yet. Alley-Cassetty ran 15 locations on separate spreadsheets and pegboards pre-FreightPOP.

modules.name: Route Optimization
modules.tag: Fewer miles, tighter windows, lower cost

problem.heading: Routes are built from memory.
problem.body: A dispatcher sequences stops by instinct. Trucks backtrack, windows get missed, and nobody can prove whether a different order of stops would have been cheaper.

benefit.heading: Optimize the sequence, then adjust by hand.
bullets: Sequence multi-stop routes for minimum miles and time
Respect delivery windows, vehicle capacity and driver availability
Balance loads across available equipment; overflow rolls to the next truck
Drag a stop to re-order it — manual adjustments are recorded
Compare optimized vs. manual plans side by side

demo.caption: A 12-stop day re-sequences to cut total drive time.

roi.proof: Sequencing happens before the day starts, not during it. The saving is drive time and fuel, computed from your own stop counts.

ev.src: No customer metric yet. Modeled from your stop counts and cost per mile.

modules.name: Driver App & POD
modules.tag: Weights, status and proof from the driver's phone

problem.heading: Proof of delivery arrives days later.
problem.body: Signed paperwork rides back in a cab, gets scanned when someone has time, and a weight captured at pickup is relayed by text or not at all. Billing and claims wait on paper.

benefit.heading: The driver closes the loop from the dock.
bullets: Free mobile app for your drivers and your carriers' drivers
Actual picked weight entered at pickup and fed straight to the record
Status updates — picked up, in transit, delivered — with comments
Photo and signature POD uploaded from the phone, instantly on the shipment
POD can be required before a driver is allowed to mark delivered

demo.caption: A driver marks delivered — photo POD and signature land on the shipment.

roi.proof: Weight and proof captured at the stop are what make same-day billing and fast claims possible.

ev.src: No customer metric yet. Modeled as days saved between delivery and invoice.

modules.name: Tracking & Notifications
modules.tag: One screen for every shipment, and customers who stop asking

problem.heading: “Where's my order?” lands on the shipping desk.
problem.body: Tracking lives in carrier portals and the ERP, so customer service asks the shipping team, who look it up by hand. Every status question costs two people time, and exceptions are found by the customer first.

benefit.heading: Every shipment, every carrier, one live view.
bullets: All in-transit freight and parcel on one screen with a calendar view
Late and at-risk shipments flagged before the customer calls
Branded, Amazon-style tracking emails to your customers, automatically
Trigger notifications on real events — only once the carrier has picked up
Give CSRs, sales and customers scoped tracking access so they self-serve

demo.caption: A late shipment flags on the board and the customer is already notified.

roi.proof: Proactive notification removes the highest-volume interruption on the shipping desk.

ev.src: Alley-Cassetty intake: the coordinator fields status calls all day. Callaway Blue had once-daily visibility only.

modules.name: Freight Invoice Audit
modules.tag: Every invoice checked against what you approved

problem.heading: Freight invoices get paid, not checked.
problem.body: Auditing means comparing a carrier bill to a quote nobody saved, line by line, across hundreds of invoices. So bills get approved on faith — and reweighs, reclasses and phantom accessorials are paid in full.

benefit.heading: Automatic variance detection on every bill.
bullets: Invoices matched to the original quote line by line, automatically
Reweighs, reclasses and unapproved accessorials flagged for dispute
EDI invoices ingested from connected carriers; broker bills uploaded
Approved invoices export to AP as bills or vendor bills
Nothing auto-pays — approval stays with your team

demo.caption: A reweigh on a carrier invoice is caught against the quoted rate and queued for dispute.

roi.proof: Invoice audit and rate shopping are the two largest components of customer savings models.

ev.src: Buffalo Seal & Gasket, closed won Dec 2025 — a single $225 carrier discrepancy, inside a $140,294 modeled annual savings case.

modules.name: Reporting & Analytics
modules.tag: Spend, service and carrier performance on demand

problem.heading: Reporting means exporting and rebuilding.
problem.body: Freight spend by lane, carrier or customer takes a data pull and a spreadsheet. By the time the analysis exists the quarter is over, and no two people build it the same way.

benefit.heading: The numbers are already in the system.
bullets: Built-in reports for spend, mode mix, carrier performance and on-time
Filter by site, customer, lane or date and export to Excel when you want to
Dashboards scoped per role so each team sees its own numbers
Direct warehouse access for Power BI and your own BI stack
Quoted vs. actual cost captured on every shipment, ready to analyze

demo.caption: Spend by carrier and lane, filtered live — no export required.

roi.proof: Carrier negotiations and mode decisions run on your own data instead of the carrier's.

ev.src: Software Advice review
ev.quote: The reporting allowed us to save considerable money by illuminating which carriers can deliver each kind of product at the lowest cost and highest service levels.

modules.name: Dock Scheduling
modules.tag: Self-service dock appointments

problem.heading: The dock runs on phone calls and a whiteboard.
problem.body: Carriers arrive whenever, the yard backs up, and detention charges pile on while labor sits idle or scrambles. Nobody upstream knows what's hitting the dock today.

benefit.heading: Let carriers book their own slots.
bullets: Publish dock availability; carriers pick and confirm their own appointments
Door and equipment needs captured at booking — forklift, liftgate, dock or drop
Appointments imported or created in bulk, per door and per site
Live schedule view for the floor — most customers run it on a screen in the warehouse
Inbound and outbound on the same calendar

demo.caption: A carrier books its own dock slot — the warehouse board updates live.

roi.proof: A known arrival schedule is what turns dock labor from reactive into planned.

ev.src: Callaway Blue intake, Jun 2026: 20 docks run on Excel and clipboards, no no-show tracking. Measured results due at their 90-day review.

wms.name: Warehouse Management
wms.intro: A warehouse layer built natively into FreightPOP — one vendor for WMS, TMS and OMS. The floor, the freight and the order share a single record, so stock and shipping never fall out of sync.

modules.name: Guided Receiving
modules.tag: Scan-based PO receipts, validated at the door
modules.cardTag: Scan-based PO receipts with expected-item validation, partial receipts with save-and-resume, and receive-to-bin or receive-to-dock flexibility.

problem.heading: Receiving runs on a clipboard and a guess.
problem.body: POs get re-keyed at the dock, big containers take days with no way to pause and resume, and over- or short-receipts surface at month-end — long after the truck is gone.

benefit.heading: Receive against the PO — validated as you scan.
bullets: Import the PO straight from TMS inbound — the truck you tracked is the receipt you work
Expected-item validation as you scan: under, complete and over flagged live
Partial receipts save and resume — supplemental receipts continue until the PO closes
Receive to a put-away bin or to the dock — your flow, either way
Approval posts a purchase receipt to your ERP automatically

demo.caption: An inbound PO is scan-received, validated against expected quantities and posted to the ERP.

roi.proof: One vendor for TMS and WMS: the shipment you tracked inbound becomes the receipt you post — zero re-keying.

ev.src: No live WMS customer metric yet — Alley-Cassetty is still in pilot.

modules.name: License Plating, Lot, and Serialization
modules.tag: Move a pallet, not a serial number
modules.cardTag: Associate items, serials and lots to one scannable license plate — move a pallet, not a serial number, with custom LP naming conventions.

problem.heading: Serialized and lot-controlled stock moves one scan at a time.
problem.body: A pallet of serialized units can't move until someone scans every serial on it, and lot codes live on paper or in a spreadsheet — so expiry, recall and traceability questions turn into a warehouse walk. Multi-section warehouses relocate stock all day, so the scanning never ends, or worse, it just gets skipped.

benefit.heading: One license plate carries the whole pallet.
bullets: Associate items, serials and lot codes to a single scannable license plate
One scan moves the pallet — every serial and lot code travels with it
Lot codes captured at receipt and carried through put-away, picks and shipment
Custom LP naming conventions: PO number, job number, or an auto-increment schema
LPs work everywhere — receipts, put-away, transfers, picks and adjustments
Print barcode labels at receipt so every pallet is scannable from day one

demo.caption: A pallet of 48 serialized units changes bins with a single license-plate scan.

roi.statLabel: moves a pallet — serials, lots and all
roi.proof: The pallet is the unit of work. Serialized and lot-controlled handling stops being the reason moves don't get recorded.

ev.src: License plating, lot and serialization — platform capability.

modules.name: Put-Away & Bin Transfers
modules.tag: Directed moves, and bins that fit how you work
modules.cardTag: Directed put-away from receiving and QA, single-item splits across bins, and bins flexible enough to be jobs, trucks or a painted line down the warehouse.

problem.heading: Stock moves, the system doesn't.
problem.body: Put-away is tribal knowledge and bin-to-bin moves happen off the record — a forklift relocates a pallet and the software never hears about it. The next picker walks to a bin that's been empty for a week.

benefit.heading: Direct every put-away, record every move.
bullets: Directed put-away from receiving and QA to the right bin
Split a single item across up to ten destination bins in one move
Consolidate many items into one bin — with live remaining-quantity checks
Bins are whatever you need: zones, trucks, jobs — even a painted line down the warehouse
License-plate aware: full pallets keep their plate through the move

demo.caption: One received item splits across a zone, a truck and a job bin — in a single recorded move.

roi.statLabel: every relocation is a scanned transaction
roi.proof: The bin the system shows is the bin the forklift finds.

ev.src: Scan-enforced moves — platform capability.

modules.name: Order Picking & Fulfillment
modules.tag: Guided picks on rugged mobile scanners
modules.cardTag: Guided sales and transfer order picking on rugged mobile scanners — bin-directed, short-key confirms, optional approval gates before writeback.

problem.heading: Pickers walk the aisles with a printout.
problem.body: Paper pick lists can't verify anything. Wrong items and short picks surface at packing — or at the customer — and nobody upstream can see what's picked and what's still waiting.

benefit.heading: Scan-guided picking from sales and transfer orders.
bullets: Open sales orders and transfer orders become picking tickets — no re-keying
Bin-directed picks on rugged mobile scanners
Short-key confirms a full bin quantity in one tap
Live line status as the pick progresses — picked, partial, waiting
Optional post and approval gates before inventory writes back

demo.caption: A sales order is scan-picked bin by bin — approved, posted and handed to the TMS to ship.

roi.statLabel: every pick, before it reaches packing
roi.proof: Errors stop at the shelf — and because WMS and TMS are one vendor, the picked order books freight without a handoff.

ev.src: Scan verification at the shelf — platform capability.

modules.name: Inventory Visibility & Adjustments
modules.tag: Live stock across every site — fixable on the spot
modules.cardTag: Real-time inventory across every site with lot and expiration tracking, on-the-spot write-offs from the scanner, and photo capture for QA and RMA.

problem.heading: Every site keeps its own version of the truth.
problem.body: Stock levels differ by system and by site. Sales promises what the warehouse doesn't have, damaged stock sits on the books for months, and nobody has proof of what condition anything arrived in.

benefit.heading: One live view — correctable where you stand.
bullets: Real-time inventory across every warehouse and site in one view
Lot and expiration tracking on every unit
Write off damaged stock from the scanner, on the spot — no back-office ticket
Photo capture on inbound and outbound for QA and vendor RMA documentation
Every adjustment is a recorded transaction that posts to your ERP

demo.caption: Water-damaged stock is written off at the bin — photo attached, adjustment posted to the ERP.

roi.proof: One vendor for WMS and TMS means the stock you see is net of everything picked, packed and already on a truck.

ev.src: Multi-site inventory — platform capability.

modules.name: Cycle Counting
modules.tag: Count continuously, not catastrophically
modules.cardTag: Scheduled ABC or full-warehouse counts, blind counting, variance review with approve-or-recount, and automatic ERP adjustment writeback.

problem.heading: The annual count shuts the building down.
problem.body: Counting means stopping — so it happens once a year, variances pile up unseen for months, and the write-off lands all at once with no way to say where accuracy went wrong.

benefit.heading: Scheduled, blind, scan-driven counts.
bullets: Scheduled counts — ABC by velocity, or full-warehouse annual
Blind counts: the counter sees the shelf, not the expected number
Variances surface immediately with approve-or-recount review
Approved adjustments write back to NetSuite automatically
No shutdown — counts run alongside daily operations

demo.caption: A blind count surfaces one variance — reviewed, approved and posted to NetSuite.

roi.proof: Small, continuous counts keep accuracy high and turn the year-end write-off into a non-event.

ev.src: No live WMS customer metric yet.

oms.name: Order Management
oms.intro: The workspace where every order arrives, gets its freight detail and is prepared — then handed to warehouse picking and to the TMS for rating and booking, with no re-entry.

modules.name: Order Management and Intake
modules.tag: Orders arrive on their own, and one queue holds them all
modules.cardTag: ERP and storefront sync on a schedule, bulk CSV import, or look up a single order by number — no re-keying to start a shipment.

problem.heading: Orders can come in from multiple systems. Without the right order management tools, shipping teams rely on spreadsheets, emails, and disconnected systems to figure out what needs to ship, when, and how.

benefit.heading: Orders arrive on their own, into one workspace.
bullets: For most customers the ERP is integrated, so released orders import automatically
The integration is configured to your rules — which orders, at which status, to which site
ERP and storefront sync on a schedule so the queue fills itself
Bulk import from a CSV template when there's no integration yet
Look up a single order by number and pull it straight into Quote & Ship
Filter and pre-set the intake trigger: status, prefix, site, required ship date
Configure the grid so each team sees only the orders it ships
One queue for sales orders, outbound, inbound, services and ROI orders
Select orders in the grid to quote, spot quote, ship, create a delivery or split

demo.caption: Orders land in the queue on their own — ERP sync, bulk import and single-order lookup.

roi.proof: The order arrives with its addresses, lines and detail already attached.

ev.src: G2 review + Callaway Blue intake (every PO re-keyed from a printed PDF)
ev.quote: An extra number here or there when manually keyed has killed us on shipments in the past. This problem is virtually eliminated now.

modules.name: Product Detail & Auto Pack
modules.tag: Catalog detail in, calculated pallets out
modules.cardTag: Items pull from the catalog with dims, weights and ERP serials; auto freight class/NMFC, saved package types, hazmat with DG paperwork — then handling units calculate themselves.

problem.heading: Most teams don't know what an order will cost to ship until after it is packed. That means freight decisions get made without one of the biggest pieces of the equation: how the order will actually be packed.

benefit.heading: Every line arrives quote-ready, and packs itself.
bullets: Items pull from the product catalog with dims, weights and ERP serial numbers
Freight class and NMFC assigned automatically; saved package types per SKU
Hazmat from the UN/NA catalog with DG paperwork and BOL language
That item detail feeds auto-pack: handling units, dims and weight calculated
Bulk pack rules define what a full case and a full pallet actually are
Item-level thresholds palletize a SKU on their own once the quantity is hit
Company-level thresholds palletize the shipment on weight, volume or box count
The routing guide then reads pallet count and box count to pick carrier and service
Fulfillment kits for orders that always ship the same way
International detail — country of origin, values, documentation — captured at entry

demo.caption: Catalog detail, predefined packages and routing guide rules — then freight cost before anything is packed.

roi.proof: Accurate class, dims and pack math at entry are what stop reclass and reweigh charges downstream.

ev.src: Catalog-driven class, NMFC and dims feeding calculated pack math — platform capability.

modules.name: Order Consolidation
modules.tag: Same destination, one load
modules.cardTag: Combine orders heading to the same destination into a single lower-cost shipment — each order keeps its own tracking.

problem.heading: Orders headed to the same place ship as separate freight. Each one looks fine on its own, so nobody sees the LTL minimums, labels, BOLs and pickups stacking up.

benefit.heading: Combine before you book, not after.
bullets: Orders matching on street, city, state and zip group into one shipment automatically
Several LTL shipments become one FTL, which is where the freight spend drops
Multi-stop truckloads built by selecting the orders and processing them as one load
Fewer labels, BOLs and carrier pickups for the warehouse to manage
Consolidate Selected works from the Order Management grid, even for a single order
Add or remove orders after the load is saved, up until pickup
Consolidated orders lock in Order Management, so nothing ships twice
Each original order keeps its own tracking and ERP writeback

demo.caption: Same-destination orders selected in the grid, consolidated into one load, rated once.

roi.proof: The saving is invisible per order and material per month.

ev.src: Shares the consolidation model — deliberately not counted twice.

modules.name: Inbound Order Management
modules.tag: Purchase orders tracked like the freight they are
modules.cardTag: Purchase orders land in the inbound queue as tracked shipments — rated, booked and visible to the dock before the truck arrives.

problem.heading: Inbound freight is a phone call and a guess at an arrival date, so the dock finds out what is coming when the truck shows up.

benefit.heading: Inbound POs live in the same system as everything else.
bullets: Purchase orders arrive in the Open Inbound Transactions tab from the ERP
Vendor freight created as a tracked inbound shipment, not an email thread
Rate and book inbound moves on your own carriers and accounts
Arrival dates and tracking visible before the truck reaches the dock
The inbound record becomes the receipt the warehouse works against

demo.caption: Inbound POs in one queue, rated, booked and tracked to the dock.

roi.statLabel: for inbound as well as outbound
roi.proof: Inbound is often the least visible half of the freight spend.

ev.src: Inbound purchase orders as tracked shipments — platform capability.

modules.tag: One record from capture to carrier

problem.heading: Three vendors own three pieces of the same order.
problem.body: The order system, the warehouse system and the freight system come from different vendors, so the order is entered once, re-entered to pick it and re-entered to ship it. Every copy drifts, the integrations between them are somebody's side job, and when the handoff breaks nobody owns it.

benefit.heading: One vendor, one record, capture to fulfillment.
bullets: Open orders flow into WMS picking with no re-keying

Partial ships and backorders stay tied to the parent order
OMS, WMS and TMS are one system, so there is no middleware to build or re-sync
One contract, one login and one team accountable for the whole handoff

erp.blurb: The standard FreightPOP ERP integration pattern: orders flow in, shipping truth flows back, and freight invoices land in AP — so the ERP stays the system of record without anyone re-keying freight data.

outFlows: Tracking numbers, carrier and ship date write back at shipment time

wms.blurb: Order and inventory sync with the warehouse system you already run — FreightPOP takes the shipping side: rating, booking, labels and tracking on the same record your WMS works.

limits: Non-standard environments go External API / custom
Pre-defined package names in FreightPOP must match the Acumatica BOXID exactly (case sensitive) or export errors; default XLARGE is sent when none mapped
Carrier selected on the Acumatica side must be a manual carrier, otherwise Acumatica's own carrier API creates a second shipment and overwrites FreightPOP tracking
No cancellation export — cancellations must be redone in Acumatica
No write-back to purchase orders
Only Open SOs and Open/unconfirmed shipments import; ship-from requires the Acumatica Warehouse ID in the FreightPOP address book company id
Acumatica package max-weight validation can reject exports
Customer IP/InstallationID changes require whitelist updates (FD 66328); trial sites allow two concurrent API users
Native plug-in needs a new customization package per Acumatica release (24R2, 25R2, 26R1 requests seen)

items.blurb: The deepest ERP integration in the catalog — bilateral sync across every transaction type NetSuite ships or receives, plus a native FreightPOP app that quotes carriers from inside the NetSuite transaction window.
inFlows: Sales Orders, Item Fulfillments, POs, Transfer Orders and RMAs import — batch or real-time, filterable by prefix and status

Live import: user enters order number(s) on Quote/Ship (POST /Order/ImportOrders)
Batch import: ERPOrdersImportService Windows task calls GET /Order/UpdateItemFulfillmentsNetSuiteParallel; first run pulls last 30 days, then last-modified-date + 1s
Export: at time of shipping (default) or after first carrier pickup/in-transit event (queue drained 8 AM and 8 PM PST)
Tracking updates: hourly on delivery day
AP export and item master sync: nightly 10 PM PDT
Change Management copy: on NetSuite update to an allocated order
scope.auth: Plug-in: NetSuite Token-Based Authentication (consumer key/secret + token ID/secret, account/realm, integration role) with HMAC-SHA256 TokenPassport over SuiteTalk SOAP (WSDL 2024.2 per engineering doc; FAQ says API version 2024_2); legacy password auth flag still exists. SuiteApp: FreightPOP API user email/password per subsidiary or for all subsidiaries; company must be API-enabled; production URL enterprise.freightpop.com, sandbox sandbox-api.freightpop.com.
api: SuiteTalk SOAP get/search/add/update — import, item fulfillment create/update, tracking update, vendor bill create (How the NetSuite Integration Works)
POST /Order/ImportOrders — live import of specific order numbers (Background Jobs & Import Architecture)
GET /Order/UpdateItemFulfillmentsNetSuiteParallel — batch import coordinator (Background Jobs & Import Architecture)
ChangeManagement/GetPendingCopies, GetComparisonData, AcceptCopy, RejectCopy, GetNotifications, SaveNotifications (Change Management page)
External API rate/getRates/V4 and getRates — used by the SuiteApp for rate shop (BF-12027, SuiteApp 1.0.263)

scope.mapping: FreightPOP SuiteApp installs from NetSuite › SuiteApps and adds a FreightPOP tab on the transaction. Production APM monitoring scripts may flag the FreightPOP script on install — exclude it from APM (seen at BayWa r.e., 2026-05). Carrier/service ↔ NetSuite Shipping Method internal ID via OrderInventoryCarrierMappings (service-specific first, then generic fallback; SCAC for broker carriers); payee values ↔ Sender/Recipient/Third Party/Payer via OrderInventoryPayeeMappings or a custom payment-terms field; subsidiary/location ID ↔ FreightPOP warehouse for ship-from; Reference 1–6 and hazmat custom fields on the integration page; deeper custom mappings stored in IntegrationMappings/CodeSnippets (TransactionType 29/30/32/33); 28 customers have hard-coded special-case logic in NetSuite.cs (Per-Customer Customization Map).
limits: Sandbox validation before production is the normal path (BayWa r.e. sandbox install 2026-02-17)
One sales transaction type per account: Sales Orders or Item Fulfillments, not both (NetSuite FAQ)
IF can be shipped once; partial shipments only when shipping from SOs (NetSuite FAQ)

items.name: QuickBooks
items.blurb: Connects shipping to your accounting — orders in, tracking and audited freight costs back, so the books reflect what actually shipped and what freight actually cost.
inFlows: Orders and customer detail import into Order Management
Addresses arrive validated at entry
outFlows: Tracking and freight cost back on the order
Approved, audited freight invoices export as bills for AP

triggers: Intuit Web Connector auto-run (recommended every 10 minutes) pulls transactions modified since last run and pushes write-backs and approved invoices
QBO: pull on order search, write-back on shipment; AR service nightly
scope.frequency: Web Connector interval set by customer (10 min recommended); ARInvoiceService daily 6:00 AM
scope.auth: Desktop: Intuit Web Connector .qwc file generated by FreightPOP plus a dedicated QuickBooks user with Sales (+Purchasing, +Accounts Payable) roles; Online: QuickBooks OAuth single sign-on
api: POST /WebServices/QuickBooksImportService.asmx — Web Connector endpoint (named in FP-6080 as a top-5 slow endpoint)
appbe /Quickbooks/SendInvoiceToQuickBook and /Quickbooks/ExportARInvoice — internal, called by ARInvoiceService
scope.mapping: Fixed transaction-type mapping with configurable target fields (Ship Via, Memo, last line, custom tracking/cost fields); customer-specific import mappings exist (Tile Redi DataExchangeValue, Elara Brands shipping notes)
limits: Web Connector must run on the machine hosting the company file; client installs fail (QBE Known Issues)
Avalara AvaTax plugin can block the connector during setup (QBE Known Issues)
Rebuilding a QB company file resets modified dates and loops the connector; use the Order Fetch Date field (Rebuilding QB Company File page, NS-1549)
Invoices approved while the connector was offline are not back-filled automatically (FD#56294, FD#65010)
Invoices without an Internal Vendor ID do not export (FD#45294)
One ERP per FreightPOP account today (FP-5486)
Multiple QB company files supported, each needs the FreightPOP user and the connector cycles through them (QuickBooks Enterprise Setup)

in: Invoices, Sales Receipts or Sales Orders (one type chosen per connection) pulled by last-modified date; initial Invoices pull is the last 6 months

Carrier + service + tracking + cost to the Memo field or to the last line description

Choice of discounted or list cost, plus optional percent or flat markup
